Gap Index for Two-Dimensional Embeddings

Source: R/gap-index.R
gap_index.Rd

Measure how the relative areas of empty regions change in an embedding. The Delaunay triangles of the embedding define the regions. Each triangle is compared with the same three observations in the reference coordinates.

Usage

gap_index(Xin, Xout, n_threads = 0, ret_extra = FALSE)

Arguments

Xin

Reference coordinates, as a dense numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows.

Xout

Two-dimensional embedding coordinates for the same observations in the same row order. Use at least three non-collinear points with distinct coordinates. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored in both inputs.

n_threads

Maximum number of threads to use. 0 or 1 runs serially.

ret_extra

Whether to return the triangles and their deformations.

Value

The scalar Gap Index. With ret_extra = TRUE, a list with gap_index, a matrix triangles of one-based row indices, and the corresponding vectors relative_area_in, relative_area_out, and signed deformation.

Details

Each area's relative share is computed by dividing by the sum of the areas of the same triangles in its own space. Both spaces use Euclidean geometry. Deformation is the output share minus the input share, divided by the larger share. Positive values indicate expansion, and negative values indicate compression. A triangle with zero area in both spaces has zero deformation. Positive total area is needed in each space.

The scalar is the mean absolute deformation weighted by each triangle's larger share across the two spaces. It ranges from 0 (no change in relative area) to 1. Relative areas are invariant to uniform rescaling of either space. A shear can preserve them while distorting shape. The triangles fill the convex hull, so regions at the boundary participate in the result. The triangulation can change with the embedding or the rows included. Requires the geometry package.

Scaling

The 2D Delaunay triangulation has a number of triangles proportional to N. Only their edge distances are computed in the two spaces. Use all eligible rows when the gaps of the full map matter. Subsetting the rows changes the triangulation and can change which gaps are visible.

Numerical failures

A nonfinite computed distance causes an error, even with finite coordinates. Finite distances alone do not guarantee accuracy at extreme coordinate scales.

References

Ros, J., Arleo, A., & Paulovich, F. (2026). Measuring Distortion in the Empty Regions of Dimensionality Reduction Scatterplots with the Gap Index. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28324 The authors provide reference code.

See also

local_procrustes(), pointwise_rnx()

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
y <- prcomp(x, rank. = 2)$x
# Use one observation per distinct location in the embedding.
keep <- !duplicated(y)
gap_index(x[keep, ], y[keep, ])
#> [1] 0.4750517
